answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. This is why the honest majority can be small yet decisive: each vote carries the weight of verifiable work, not just the noise of a large flock.. The defense holds because trust accrues slowly and is lost fast, so a farm that ever submits a copied answer destroys the value of that identity. Consider a sparrow as the anchor of the cost.
